findings.title: Adjusting for total energy decides what a nutrient's coefficient means.
findings.detail: `kcal` is total energy. `protein`, `sugar`, `carb`, `fat_total`, `fat_sat` and 2 more carry energy, and each correlates 0.67 to 0.88 with `kcal`.
findings.why_it_matters: Adjusting for total energy makes a nutrient's coefficient a substitution: more of it in place of other energy at the same total. Leaving energy out, or partitioning it, asks about adding energy instead. The two answer different questions (Tomova et al. 2022), so which to ask is the study's choice and the method follows from it. For prediction, models that keep total energy predict alike.

evidence.source: research/NUTRITION_PACK.md#04 · Energy adjustment — the methodological signature

base.estimand: The standard model's substitution, in each nutrient's own units: the residuals and total energy span the same model as the nutrients and total energy, so each coefficient is the standard model's exactly (McCullough & Byrd 2023, AJE 192(11):1801-1805). With protein, carbohydrate and fat all in the model, each coefficient is a substitution in place of the energy sources not in the model: alcohol, other. carb sits beside its own parts sugar, so its coefficient is the remaining carbohydrate (holding sugar fixed): the carbohydrate in none of them, not total carbohydrate. fat_total sits beside its own parts fat_sat, fat_mon and fat_poly, so its coefficient is the remaining fat (holding fat_sat, fat_mon, fat_poly fixed): the fat in none of them, not total fat.
warnings: sugar is a part of carb: carb's coefficient is the remainder (holding sugar fixed), not total carb; leave it out to estimate the total. A substitution through carb moves it in proportion, and never pairs carb with its own part.

fat_sat, fat_mon, fat_poly are parts of fat_total: fat_total's coefficient is the remainder (holding fat_sat, fat_mon, fat_poly fixed), not total fat_total; leave them out to estimate the total. A substitution through fat_total moves them in proportion, and never pairs fat_total with its own part.

base.estimand: The average change in predicted glucose when k kcal move from protein to sugar, their parts or totals moving with them and every other input, total energy included, left as it was.
base.note: Total energy was held fixed by assumption: intake can rise or fall, so keeping the total constant is a modeling choice, not a property of the data. Rows whose shifted protein or sugar would leave the observed range or go negative, or whose share of energy from either (of kcal) would leave the range of that share observed, are left out at that k, and the curve stops at the first k where fewer than 50% of rows remain; that 50% floor (min_support) is a practitioner convention, not a sourced threshold. The curve stopped at k = 300 kcal, where 39% of rows remained on support. Each k averages over its own on-support rows, so the rows behind the curve change with k; the fixed-population curve averages over the same 1,722 rows, those on support at every k up to 200 kcal. On every row, sugar is part of carb, so carb moved with it by the same amount while its other parts held. The model holds protein, carb and fat_total; alcohol and other energy make up the rest of total energy, 1% of it on average, and more than 10% on 193 of 2,396 rows. Total energy carries them as one composite, so the curve carries their confounding (Tomova, Gilthorpe & Tennant 2022: "wherever ≥2 components are involved in the substitution, there is scope for composite variable bias unless the individual effects are estimated"); add the remaining sources to the model to remove it. protein is read in grams by its values (the Atwater identity holds with total energy), at 4 kcal per gram. sugar moves at 4 kcal per unit, recorded in g: carbohydrate at 4 kcal/g.
